### Project Name

ContextForge

### Project Description

An open source registry and proxy that federates MCP, A2A, and REST/gRPC APIs with centralized governance, discovery, and observability. Optimizes Agent & Tool calling, facilitates reference implementations and supports plugins. ContextForge provides users with fast time-to-value, and we have invested significant focus on the needs of both the developer as well as the organizations looking to use AI responsibly.

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

ContextForge is designed as an extensible agent infrastructure layer rather than a closed gateway. Its plugin architecture allows developers and the community to add transports, protocols, security controls, integrations, and governance capabilities without modifying the core platform. With 40+ plugins already available and a growing ecosystem for MCP servers, agent runtimes, and developer tools, ContextForge can evolve alongside the rapidly changing MCP, A2A, and agentic AI ecosystem in support of the AAIF mission.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

ContextForge supports the emerging AAIF Product Development Lifecycle by providing a consistent governance and integration layer from development through production. Developers can build and test MCP servers, tools, and agents against a common gateway; security, authentication, policy, and observability can be incorporated before release; and the same governed infrastructure can then be deployed and monitored in production. 
ContextForge focuses on registry, discovery, federation and governance, while nascent AAIF hosted project AgentGateway is more of a high performance traffic/data plane. There is some competitive overlap between the two, however this is a large and rapidly evolving ecosystem with room for collaboration, interoperability and competition. We would also welcome the formation of an Agentic AI Gateway Working Group or Special Interest Group (SIG) to provide additional focus.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

Typical use cases include a developer who wants to expose tools, prompts or resources via MCP or A2A; a team that is building a client or agent framework that utilizes those protocols; an enterprise that wants to consume Gateway APIs from an LLM agent, browser app, or CLI tool. ContextForge has over 4.1K stars, ~70 contributors, 2.6M DLs as of 17 July 2026.

### External Project Dependencies

Core Runtime Dependencies include MCP SDK (MIT), Pydantic & Pydantic-Settings (MIT), HTTP Client (BSD3) and Instrumentator (ISC).

### Maintainers & Contributors

ContextForge started as a passion project by an individual in IBM consulting (Mihai Creviti - crivetimihai) who saw the potential of MCP and did most of the original coding in 2025 and early 2026. We started hiring a team of developers based in the IBM SW Lab in Dublin, Ireland who have been making substantial improvements to the codebase. IBM is committed to continuing to rapidly evolve the open source project, and we are currently pursing some other organizations to become core maintainers as appropriate. Complete list of maintainers and contributors here: https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/graphs/contributors?from=5%2F9%2F2026

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

IBM consulting's laser-focus on the immediate and future enterprise requirements of our clients drove most all of the early development of ContextForge during its first year of existence. The project continues to benefit from many of our early adopters, and we have clients using CF in production today. The immediate leadership team of ContextForge is Wayne Leone, Jonathan Springer, Brian Hussey, Jeffrey Borek.

### Security

CF uses a "defense-in-depth" and "secure-by-design" philosophy to protect Model Context Protocol (MCP) data flows and AI infrastructure. As a secure registry and proxy, the project mitigates the risks of unauthorized tool execution and sensitive data leaks across AI clients. https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/blob/main/SECURITY.md

### Additional Information

For more than 30 years, IBM has been a committed participant in the open technology and open source ecosystem. From our early investments in Linux, Apache and Eclipse to our leadership across cloud native, open source security and other emerging technologies, IBM has consistently recognized that the most durable innovation comes from open collaboration, open standards and open governance. IBM helped establish and grow foundational communities, contributed significant engineering resources and intellectual property, and has continued to be one of the world’s largest enterprise contributors to open source.
This philosophy remains particularly important as open source expands into AI and agentic technologies. IBM’s objective is not simply to advance its own technology agenda, but to help build healthy, sustainable and secure communities that can support the entire AI ecosystem. We believe our role is to bring engineering, resources, expertise and enterprise requirements to the table, listen to what the community needs, and work collaboratively to address shared challenges. Ultimately, IBM’s success in open source is inseparable from the health of the communities we depend upon—and being a good open source citizen means helping those communities succeed, not just helping ourselves.
